measures.what: outside diameter of the outer ring — put the caliper's flat jaws on the widest ring (the outer race), not the little inner ring, and squeeze gently square across the middle. Also give me its width across the faces
measures.reply: bearing od: about 22 mm (outside); bearing width: about 7 mm; bearing bore: about 8 mm (the hole)

measures.what: overall length under the head, the diameter of the smooth unthreaded part right under the head, the diameter of the threads, and how far from the head the threads start (i.e. is it threaded all the way to the shank?)

measures.item: the door hanger bracket (the metal fork the old wheel was bolted to)
measures.what: the inside spacing between the two flat plates the wheel sits between (outside-to-outside of the wheel space), the diameter of the hole the bolt goes through, and how many of these brackets per door

measures.item: the track/channel the wheel rolls in, at the top of the door frame
measures.what: the inside width between the two walls of the channel, the width of the flat floor the wheel runs on, and the height of the channel walls
measures.reply: I can't measure that. Use your best judgment.

measures.what: the tread — the surface that touches the track: is it flat, barrel/round-crowned, or does it have a groove running around the middle? Give me its width, and if there's a groove its width and depth
measures.reply: I can't measure that. Use your best judgment.

measures.what: its weight if you can guess it (lift one corner and judge), and the width of the slot or opening in the bottom of the door that the hanger bracket passes through
measures.reply: I can't measure that. Use your best judgment.

measures.item: the metal hanger bracket the broken wheel came off (hold it flat on the table)
measures.what: the gap between the two inner faces of the plates that the wheel sat between — slide a ruler or a stack of coins into the gap. I need it to within ~0.5 mm (e.g. "16 mm", "17 mm")
measures.reply: I can't measure that. Use your best judgment.

measures.item: the track on the floor or the top of the frame that the wheel rolls in
measures.what: two things: (a) is the running surface flat, or does it have a raised rib/ridge down the middle? (b) if there IS a rib, how tall is it above the floor of the channel, roughly, in mm
measures.reply: I can't measure that. Use your best judgment.

limitations.wanted: A steel axle sleeve/spacer between the two bearings, skateboard-style, so the clamp load never reaches the printed plastic
limitations.blocked_by: No sleeve or standoff in the hardware list, and a printed sleeve cannot pass through the 22 mm bearing bore anyway — the only through-hole available is the 8 mm bolt, which is also the axle
limitations.why: It would let the bracket plates clamp the bolt/sleeve instead of clamping the bearing faces, removing thrust drag and keeping PLA creep out of the load path

limitations.blocked_by: The person could not measure the hanger fork gap, the track channel, or the old wheel's tread with any tool available to them
limitations.wanted: A measured fork gap and track profile to set the wheel width and tread form exactly
limitations.why: So I could confirm the 16.0 mm overall width and the centre groove rather than inferring them from the old wheel's stated size; the submission hedges with a fit coupon and a pre-assembly fit check
